Why Image Format Matters for Website Speed and SEO

Every image format uses a different compression method. Some are decades old and inefficient by today's standards (like BMP), while newer formats such as AVIF use modern compression algorithms that can shrink file size by 50% or more without visible quality loss.

attrs.content:
• Pros: Universally supported, good compression for photos.
  • Cons: Lossy compression degrades quality if over-compressed; no transparency support.
  • Best for: Photos, banners, hero images where transparency isn't needed.
PNG (.png)
A lossless format that preserves quality perfectly, including transparency.
  • Pros: Supports transparency, no quality loss, great for graphics with sharp edges.
  • Cons: Much larger file sizes than JPEG or WebP for photos.
  • Best for: Logos, icons, screenshots, graphics with text or flat colors.
WebP (.webp)
Google's format, built specifically for the web. Offers both lossy and lossless compression.
  • Pros: 25–35% smaller than JPEG at similar quality, supports transparency and animation, supported by all modern browsers.
  • Cons: Slightly less universal support in very old browsers (rarely an issue today).
  • Best for: Almost everything — it's the current default recommendation for most websites.
